peopleAlsoAsk.question: What are the AAP guidelines for physical activity?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Kids aged 3-5 need at least 3 hours of physical activity per day, or about 15 minutes every hour they are awake. Kids 6 years and older need 60 minutes of moderate to vigorous physical activity on most days of the week.Aug 5, 2020
peopleAlsoAsk.title: Making Physical Activity a Way of Life: AAP Policy Explained

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What are the AHA recommendations for resistance training?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Add moderate- to high-intensity muscle-strengthening activity (such as resistance or weights) on at least 2 days per week. Spend less time sitting. Even light-intensity activity can offset some of the risks of being sedentary. Gain even more benefits by being active at least 300 minutes (5 hours) per week.Jan 19, 2024

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What are the ACSM recommendations for resistance training?
What are the guidelines for resistance training in youth?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Beginners should use resistance between 50-70 percent of 1RM (one rep maximum) for 10-15 repetitions. One to two sets per muscle group should be used for all major muscles. As youth progress to become advanced lifters, they can use 70-85 percent 1RM for 6-10 repetitions.
